questions.question: The Battle of Talikota (1565), which dealt a decisive blow to the Vijayanagara Empire, was fought against the combined armies of four Deccan Sultanates. Which of the following was NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: The Shahi alliance at Talikota comprised Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bijapur and Golconda. Mewar was a Rajput kingdom in north-western India, unconnected with the Deccan sultanates.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's works in 14th-century Delhi:
1. He set up the Firoz Shah Kotla, where he installed an Ashokan pillar brought from Topra in Ambala.
2. He repaired the Qutub Minar after it was damaged by lightning.
3. He founded the fortified city of Tughlaqabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq erected the Firoz Shah Kotla with the Topra Ashokan pillar and repaired the Qutub Minar after lightning damage. Tughlaqabad was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, not by Firoz Shah.

questions.question:
Match the dance forms (List-I) with their states (List-II):
List-I: (a) Sattriya (b) Kuchipudi (c) Yakshagana (d) Garba
List-II: 1. Andhra Pradesh 2. Assam 3. Gujarat 4. Karnataka
questions.explanation: Sattriya is the classical dance of Assam (from the sattra monasteries), Kuchipudi of Andhra Pradesh, Yakshagana is the dance-drama of Karnataka, and Garba is the folk dance of Gujarat.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kangra Fort : Katoch dynasty
2. Gwalior Fort : Sher Shah Suri (Sur dynasty)
3. Chittorgarh Fort : Guhila dynasty of Mewar
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Kangra Fort is associated with the Katoch dynasty; Gwalior Fort passed to Sher Shah Suri (who died there in 1545); Chittorgarh was the citadel of the Guhila dynasty of Mewar. All three pairs are correctly matched.

questions.question:
With reference to legislative procedure, consider the following statements:
1. Article 200 lists the Governor's options when a Bill passed by the State Legislature is presented: assent, withhold assent, return it (if not a Money Bill), or reserve it for the President's consideration.
2. Article 201 deals with Bills reserved by the Governor for the President's consideration.
3. Article 111 contains the parallel procedure for the President's assent to Bills passed by Parliament.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Article 200 (Governor's options on a State Bill), Article 201 (Bills reserved for the President) and Article 111 (President's assent to Union Bills) are all correctly described.

questions.question: The 58th Jnanpith Award (for 2023), announced in 2024, was shared by two writers. Which languages do Gulzar and Jagadguru Rambhadracharya represent respectively?
questions.explanation: Gulzar, the Urdu poet-lyricist, and Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, the Sanskrit scholar-poet, jointly received the 58th Jnanpith Award for 2023 (announced in February 2024).

questions.question:
IRDAI has proposed a 'Bima Trinity' to expand insurance coverage in India. Consider the following statements:
1. Bima Sugam is envisaged as a one-stop digital marketplace for insurance products and services.
2. Bima Vistaar is designed as a bundled product for rural areas covering life, health and property risks together.
3. Bima Vahak is a field force intended to strengthen last-mile insurance delivery, with a focus on women.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Bima Trinity comprises Bima Sugam (digital marketplace/platform), Bima Vistaar (bundled life-health-property product for rural coverage) and Bima Vahak (women-centric last-mile field force). All three statements are correct.

questions.question: Gyanesh Kumar took charge as Chief Election Commissioner of India on 19 February 2025. Which one of the following statements about his appointment is correct?
options: A) He is the 25th CEC and was appointed under the pre-2023 convention
B) He previously served as Chief Secretary of Haryana
C) He is the 26th CEC and the first to be appointed under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment) Act, 2023
D) He belongs to the 1988 batch of the Bihar cadre of the IAS
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar (1988-batch IAS, Kerala cadre) became the 26th CEC and the first selected under the 2023 Act. Vivek Joshi, Haryana's Chief Secretary, was appointed Election Commissioner alongside him, and Kumar's cadre is Kerala, not Bihar.

questions.question: The NISAR satellite, launched on 30 July 2025 by GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota, is notable primarily because:
options: A) It carries a dual-frequency synthetic aperture radar (NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band) — the first satellite to image Earth with a dual-band SAR
B) It is India's first dedicated military reconnaissance satellite
C) It studies exoplanet atmospheres from a Sun-synchronous orbit
D) It carried Chandrayaan-4 modules towards the Moon
questions.explanation: NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is the first satellite to observe Earth with a dual-band SAR — NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band sharing a 12-metre reflector — designed to detect subtle changes in land and ice surfaces. It was placed in a 743 km Sun-synchronous orbit.

questions.question: Who won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy (ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year) for 2024, and which achievement marked his year?
options: A) Mohammed Shami — leading ODI wicket-taker of 2024
B) Jasprit Bumrah — highest Test wicket-taker of 2024 with 71 wickets
C) Ravichandran Ashwin — most Test wickets among spinners in 2024
D) Travis Head — highest Test run-scorer of 2024
questions.explanation: Jasprit Bumrah won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy as ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year 2024 (announced January 2025) after taking 71 Test wickets — the most in 2024 — and was also named Men's Test Cricketer of the Year.

questions.question: Amelia Kerr of New Zealand won the Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy as ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year 2024. Which Indian batter was named ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year in the same awards?
questions.explanation: Smriti Mandhana, with 747 ODI runs in 2024 at an average of 57.46, was named ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year — her second such award after 2018.

questions.question: The Hanle Dark Sky Reserve (HDSR), India's first dark-sky reserve notified in December 2022, lies within which region, and through which partnership is it operated?
options: A) Changthang Wildlife Reserve in Ladakh; MoU between UT Ladakh, LAHDC Leh and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics
B) Spiti valley of Himachal Pradesh; MoU with IUCAA, Pune
C) Rann of Kutch, Gujarat; MoU with PRL, Ahmedabad
D) Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu; MoU with IIA and TIFR
questions.explanation: HDSR occupies a roughly 22 km radius around Hanle inside the Changthang Wildlife Reserve in eastern Ladakh. It was notified in December 2022 and is operated through an MoU between UT Ladakh, LAHDC Leh and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru.

questions.question: The Shahi Jama Masjid of Sambhal, which remained in the news through 2024–25 over a court-ordered survey and subsequent ASI-related directions, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Sambhal lies in western Uttar Pradesh. A local court-ordered survey of the mosque in November 2024 led to tensions, and the Allahabad High Court later directed ASI whitewashing of the mosque exterior, which the Supreme Court declined to interfere with in April 2025.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of (Report/Index : Publishing organisation) is correctly matched?
options: A) Global Hunger Index : World Bank
B) Human Development Report : World Economic Forum
C) World Happiness Report : UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network
D) Global Innovation Index : International Monetary Fund
questions.explanation: The World Happiness Report is published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network. The Global Hunger Index is brought out by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, the Human Development Report by UNDP, and the Global Innovation Index by WIPO.

questions.question: In the Global Innovation Index 2024, released by WIPO, India ranked 39th — up from 40th in 2023. Which of the following was NOT among the top five economies in GII 2024?
questions.explanation: The GII 2024 top five were Switzerland (1st), Sweden (2nd), the United States (3rd), Singapore (4th) and the United Kingdom (5th). Japan stood 7th, so it was not in the top five.

questions.question: Find the next term of the series: 3, 10, 29, 66, 127, ?
questions.explanation: Consecutive differences are 7, 19, 37, 61; the second differences are 12, 18, 24 (an AP with common difference 6), so the next second difference is 30, giving the next first difference 91. Hence 127 + 91 = 218. Equivalently, the nth term is n³ + 2.

questions.question: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A and B are siblings, so C (B's mother) is also A's mother. D, being C's father, is A's maternal grandfather. Hence A is D's granddaughter. (E's details are extra information.)

questions.question: A delivery rider starts from his depot and rides 4 km north. He turns right and rides 3 km, then turns right again and rides 4 km, and finally turns left and rides 12 km. How far is he from the depot?
questions.explanation: Track directions: 4 km north, then 3 km east, then 4 km south (which cancels the 4 km north exactly), then 12 km further east. Net displacement = 15 km due east, which is the straight-line distance from the depot.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: ACE, BDF, CEG, DHI
questions.explanation: ACE, BDF and CEG each consist of letters spaced exactly two apart (A→C→E, B→D→F, C→E→G). In DHI the spacing breaks (D→H skips three letters). Hence DHI is the odd group.

questions.question: In a certain code language, MONKEY is written as NPOLFZ. How is DONKEY written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of the word is shifted one place forward in the alphabet: M→N, O→P, N→O, K→L, E→F, Y→Z, giving NPOLFZ. Applying the same rule to DONKEY: D→E, O→P, N→O, K→L, E→F, Y→Z, which gives EPOLFZ.

questions.question: Symphony : Composer :: Novel : ?
questions.explanation: A symphony is created by a composer; similarly, a novel is created by a novelist. The relationship is 'work : its creator'.

questions.question:
In a certain code language:
'bright students learn fast' is written as 'pa da ni'
'fast cars are costly' is written as 'zo da ki tu'
'students are bright' is written as 'ni pa zo'
What is the code for 'fast'?
questions.explanation: Sentence 1 and sentence 2 share exactly one word, 'fast', and their codes share exactly one symbol, 'da'. Hence 'fast' = 'da'. (From sentences 1 and 3, 'students' and 'bright' correspond to 'pa' and 'ni' in some order; 'zo' is 'are'.)

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the votes polled were invalid. The winner secured 60% of the valid votes and won by 9,600 votes. The total number of votes polled was:
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 80% of total T. Winner secured 60% of valid votes, so the loser got 40%; the margin is 20% of valid votes = 0.2 × 0.8T = 0.16T = 9,600, giving T = 60,000.

questions.question: A and B enter a partnership, with A investing ₹8,000 for 12 months and B investing ₹12,000 for 12 months. After 6 months, C joins with ₹15,000 for the remaining 6 months. Out of an annual profit of ₹9,900, what is C's share?
How many numbers between 200 and 500 are divisible by 13?
questions.explanation: The first multiple of 13 after 200 is 208 (13 × 16) and the last before 500 is 494 (13 × 38). Count = 38 − 16 + 1 = 23.

questions.question: 12 men can complete a piece of work in 25 days, and 18 women can complete the same work in 25 days. In how many days will 4 men and 9 women complete the work?
questions.explanation: Total work = 18 women × 25 days = 450 woman-days, so 1 man = 18/12 = 1.5 women. 4 men + 9 women = 6 + 9 = 15 women. Time = 450/15 = 30 days.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 3 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both balls are of the same colour?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes: C(4,2) + C(5,2) + C(3,2) = 6 + 10 + 3 = 19. Total outcomes: C(12,2) = 66. Probability = 19/66.

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two positive integers are 6 and 306 respectively. If one of the integers is 102, the other integer is:
questions.explanation: Product of the two numbers = HCF × LCM = 6 × 306 = 1,836. Other number = 1,836 ÷ 102 = 18. Check: HCF(102, 18) = 6 and LCM(102, 18) = 306. ✓

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself in 16 years at simple interest. The annual rate of interest is:
questions.explanation: Tripling means the interest earned equals twice the principal: 2P = P × r × 16/100, so r = 200/16 = 12.5% per annum.

questions.question: In a class of 15 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 8 : 7. The average score of the boys is 52 and that of the girls is 37. The average score of the whole class is:
questions.explanation: Boys = 8, girls = 7. Total score = 8 × 52 + 7 × 37 = 416 + 259 = 675. Class average = 675/15 = 45.

questions.question: How many complete revolutions does a wheel of diameter 70 cm make in travelling a distance of 2.2 km? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Circumference = πd = (22/7) × 0.70 m = 2.2 m. Distance = 2.2 km = 2,200 m. Number of revolutions = 2,200/2.2 = 1,000.

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are 12 cm, 9 cm and 8 cm respectively. The length of its diagonal is:

The table shows the number of two-wheellers (in thousands) produced by two factories, P and Q, in four quarters of a year:
Quarter:        Q1    Q2    Q3    Q4
Factory P:      120   150   180   150
Factory Q:      100   140   160   100
Factory P's production in Q3 exceeds its production in Q1 by what per cent?
questions.explanation: P's Q3 production = 180 thousand; Q1 = 120 thousand. Increase = 60 thousand; percentage = (60/120) × 100 = 50%.

questions.question: If a − b = 3 and a² + b² + ab = 39, then a³ − b³ equals:
questions.explanation: Using a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) = 3 × 39 = 117.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 9?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) — 4 out of 36. Probability = 4/36 = 1/9.

questions.question: In a group of 80 students, 45 opt for Mathematics, 38 opt for Physics, and 12 opt for both. How many students opt for neither subject?
questions.explanation: Students opting for at least one subject = 45 + 38 − 12 = 71. Neither = 80 − 71 = 9.

questions.question: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V sit in a row facing north. R sits exactly in the middle. Q sits immediately to the left of R. T sits at the extreme right end. V sits second to the right of R. U sits adjacent to V. P and S occupy the remaining seats, with S not at the extreme left end. Who sits second from the left end?
questions.explanation: Positions 1–7: R = 4, Q = 3, T = 7, V = 6 (second right of R), U = 5 (adjacent to V). Remaining seats 1 and 2 go to P and S; since S is not at the extreme left, S = 2 and P = 1. So S sits second from the left end.

questions.question: 15 August 1947 fell on a Friday. On which day of the week was 26 January 1950?
questions.explanation: Days from 15 Aug 1947 to 26 Jan 1950: rest of 1947 = 138 days; 1948 (leap) = 366; 1949 = 365; 1950 up to 26 Jan = 26. Total = 895 days. 895 mod 7 = 6, so the day is Friday + 6 = Thursday.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 40 minutes past 6?

Six managers A, B, C, D, E and F each conduct a training session on a different day from Monday to Saturday of one week. The following information is given:
1. E conducts the session on Monday.
2. B conducts the session on Wednesday.
3. D conducts the session on Saturday.
4. C conducts the session exactly three days before F.
5. A conducts the session immediately before F.
Who conducts the session on Friday?
questions.explanation: Days 1–6 (Monday–Saturday): E = 1, B = 3, D = 6. The pair (C, F) must satisfy F − C = 3 using the remaining days {2, 4, 5}; the only fit is C = 2 (Tuesday) and F = 5 (Friday), which then forces A = 4 (Thursday). Hence F conducts the session on Friday.

questions.question:
Four friends — Amit, Bina, Carlos and Divya — live in four different cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata) and practise four different professions (Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer and Teacher), one each.
1. Amit is the Lawyer.
2. Divya is the Doctor.
3. The Doctor lives in Kolkata.
4. Bina lives in Chennai.
5. The Engineer lives in Delhi.
6. Carlos does not live in Mumbai.
7. The Teacher lives in Mumbai.
In which city does the Lawyer live?
questions.explanation: Amit = Lawyer, Divya = Doctor → Bina and Carlos are the Engineer and Teacher. Divya (Doctor) lives in Kolkata and the Teacher lives in Mumbai. If Bina were the Engineer she would live in Delhi, contradicting her living in Chennai — so Bina is the Teacher (Mumbai) and Carlos is the Engineer (Delhi). The remaining city, Chennai, is Amit's (the Lawyer's).

questions.question:
Statements: All notebooks are pens. Some pens are pencils.
Conclusions: I. Some notebooks are pencils. II. Some pencils are pens.
Which of the conclusions follows?
options: A) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Conclusion II is the valid converse of 'Some pens are pencils'. Conclusion I does not necessarily follow: the pencils may overlap only that part of 'pens' which lies outside 'notebooks'. Hence only II follows.

questions.question: A jeweller has three drawers, each containing exactly two gold coins. One drawer has two ₹1 coins, one has two ₹2 coins, and one has one ₹1 and one ₹2 coin. Each drawer carries a label, but all three labels are wrong. The jeweller may open one drawer and take out exactly one coin (without looking inside the drawer). From which drawer should he pick the coin so that he can determine the contents of all three drawers?
options: A) The drawer labelled 'one ₹1 and one ₹2 coin'
D) Any drawer will work equally well
questions.explanation: The drawer labelled 'one ₹1 and one ₹2 coin' cannot actually be the mixed drawer (its label is wrong), so it is a pure drawer. The single coin drawn reveals which pure pair it holds, fixing that drawer completely. The other two labels are also wrong, so the remaining pure-labelled drawer cannot hold its labelled pair and must be the mixed drawer; the last drawer is forced. No other choice guarantees full deduction.

questions.question: Photographic film darkens when exposed to light because of which chemical change?
options: A) Oxidation of silver nitrate to silver oxide
B) Decomposition of silver chloride into chlorine gas only
C) Combination of silver with sulphur to form silver sulphide
D) Reduction of silver bromide to metallic silver
questions.explanation: Light supplies energy for the photolytic decomposition of silver bromide (2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂); the finely divided metallic silver so formed darkens the film.

questions.question: Which component of blood plays the primary role in clotting at the site of an injury?
questions.explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) accumulate at the injury site and, together with clotting factors in plasma, form the clot that seals the wound. White blood cells fight infection, and red blood cells carry oxygen.

questions.question: A person suffers from hypermetropia (far-sightedness) and cannot see nearby objects clearly. Which corrective lens is prescribed, and what does it do?
options: A) Convex lens; it converges incoming rays so the image forms on the retina
B) Concave lens; it diverges incoming rays before they enter the eye
C) Bifocal lens only; it corrects both near and distant vision defects simultaneously
D) Cylindrical lens; it corrects the uneven curvature of the cornea
questions.explanation: In hypermetropia the eye's near point recedes because incoming rays focus behind the retina. A convex (converging) lens pre-converges the rays so that the final image forms on the retina. Concave lenses correct myopia, and cylindrical lenses correct astigmatism.

questions.question: Industrial effluent containing methylmercury enters a lake. The lake supports: plankton → small fish → large predatory fish → humans who eat the fish. In which part of this system would the highest concentration of mercury per unit of body tissue be found, and why?
options: A) Plankton, because they are the first to absorb the effluent directly
B) Lake water, because mercury remains dissolved and does not enter organisms
C) Small fish, because they have the fastest metabolism
D) Top consumers (humans), because mercury biomagnifies up the food chain
questions.explanation: Methylmercury is not readily excreted and accumulates in tissue. Each predator absorbs the accumulated burden of all its prey, so concentration rises at every trophic level — a process called biomagnification — making top consumers (here, humans) carry the highest tissue concentration.

questions.question: Ocean acidification, which threatens coral reefs and shell-forming marine organisms, results primarily from:
options: A) Deposition of sulphate aerosols from volcanic eruptions on the ocean surface
B) Release of methane hydrates from the seabed
C) Increased dissolution of atmospheric carbon dioxide in seawater, forming carbonic acid
D) Runoff of nitrogenous fertilisers from coastal agriculture
questions.explanation: As the oceans absorb excess atmospheric CO₂, the gas reacts with seawater to form carbonic acid, lowering the pH (acidification) and reducing the carbonate ions that corals and shellfish need. Fertiliser runoff instead causes eutrophication, and methane hydrates are a separate deep-ocean concern.

questions.question: Iron-deficiency anaemia is among the most common nutritional disorders in India. Iron deficiency leads to anaemia primarily because iron is an essential component of:
options: B) White blood cells, which fight infection
C) Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying pigment of red blood cells
D) Blood plasma, which transports nutrients
questions.explanation: Iron sits at the centre of the haem group of haemoglobin, the pigment that binds oxygen in red blood cells. Without enough iron, haemoglobin synthesis falls, oxygen transport drops, and the characteristic fatigue and pallor of anaemia follow.

questions.question: A wooden block floats in water with exactly three-fourths of its volume submerged. The block is now moved to another liquid of density 600 kg/m³ (the block's density is unchanged, and water's density is 1000 kg/m³). What will happen?
options: A) It will sink, because floating would require more than its full volume to be submerged
B) It will float with half of its volume submerged
C) It will float exactly as before, with three-fourths submerged
D) It will float with its entire volume submerged but still be neutrally buoyant
questions.explanation: From the first case, the block's density = 0.75 × 1000 = 750 kg/m³. In the new liquid, floating would require a submerged fraction = 750/600 = 1.25 — more than the whole block — which is impossible. Since the block is denser than the liquid (750 > 600), it sinks.
